topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Genetic origins and cellular context of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arising in susceptible cells can drive clonal evolution toward cancer within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and evidence for their contribution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the contribution of environmental exposures to cancer risk and the evidence for distinguishing that contribution from chance and inherited predisposition.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between infection and cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage by environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage and mutations, showing how their effects depend on their molecular activity within the body.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutagenic initiation may require subsequent tumour-promoting conditions for cancer to develop.

topics.label: Host susceptibility and recap of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the host tissue's developmental state shapes susceptibility to carcinogens and consolidate the preceding account of context-dependent carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Identifying carcinogenic exposures and assessing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how evidence of carcinogenic exposure and activity is obtained, emphasizing the capabilities and limitations of the available methods.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarizing its conclusions and placing environmental cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
